subject: ACME POC: Evaluation plan & methodology alignment

Subject: ACME POC: Evaluation plan & methodology alignment

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps for the POC so we can align on success criteria and the evaluation methodology.

Call recap (high level):
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for ACME's customer support summarization flow (40M tokens / month estimate).
- Key success metrics: quality (F1/ROUGE-style rubrics agreed below), latency (95th percentile < 300ms for single-turn), and cost per 1k tokens in production target <$1.20.
- Stakeholders: Alex (Engineering lead), Priya (Product owner), Marissa (REPs), Dylan (Sales), Rishi (SE).

Proposed POC plan & owners (attached spreadsheet has details):
1) Week 0-1: Data collection & scope — ACME provides 1k representative transcripts + 50 critical edge cases (owner: Priya).
2) Week 2: Offline eval run against curated holdout set — blueprint and rubric (owner: Rishi).
3) Week 3: Shadow (online) run — mirror traffic to Redwood gateway, measure latency & throughput, compare outputs to baseline (owner: Dylan/Rishi).
4) Week 4: Joint review & go/no-go based on rubric thresholds; finalize rollout recommendations (owner: Alex/Priya).

Evaluation methodology notes (for alignment):
- Offline evals: deterministic scoring on curated holdout using a human-graded rubric (clarify grading scale below). Good for correctness/regression detection, prompt tuning.
- Online shadow: required to measure performance at scale (latency, throughput, error modes) and to catch distribution drift under real traffic patterns.

Draft grading rubric (Rishi to formalize):
- Relevance/accuracy (0-3): 3 = fully correct, 2 = minor omission, 1 = partially correct, 0 = incorrect/misleading.
- Conciseness (0-2): 2 = concise, 1 = verbose but correct, 0 = irrelevant.
- Hallucination severity (0-2): 0 = severe hallucination, 2 = none.
- Overall pass threshold = >=7/7 for green, 5-6 = amber (requires mitigation), <=4 = red.

Attachments: acme-poc-eval-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet, ~54KB) and Redwood POC SLA (PDF).

Next steps: please reply with confirmation of owners and any changes to success metrics. If you agree, I'll book the kickoff for Tuesday (Week 0).

Thanks,

Thanks — adding details on evaluation methodology and the rubric based on your comments. Please find the summary below and I've attached the initial rubric to the Drive link in the thread.

Offline evals (recommended first step):
- Purpose: fast iteration over prompt variants and model configs; high signal on correctness and regression.
- Process: we run inference on the 1k transcripts; outputs are scored by a 3-person human panel using the rubric below. We also compute automated metrics (ROUGE, BLEU where applicable) to aid triage.
- Deliverables: annotated scoring sheet, scatter of model vs metric, suggested prompt tweaks.

Online shadow (recommended in Week 3):
- Purpose: measure operational performance (latency, error rate), real-time degradation modes, and emergent behaviour under real traffic.
- Mode: mirror requests to Redwood via a non-blocking proxy; Redwood returns responses, but we do not show to end users. Overhead: typically 5-15% additional RPS depending on sampling. We can start with 10% sampling.
- Data handling: we will respect your redaction rules; any PHI items should be redacted before sending or sent via a private endpoint with customer-managed KMS (we can enable).

Rubric (draft):
- Relevance/Accuracy (0-3) — details as Marissa outlined.
- Conciseness (0-2).
- Hallucination severity (0-2).
- PHI redaction pass (0/1) — fail if 0.
- Automated confidence check (0/1) — bonus point if model provides high-confidence marker and matches human score.

Pass thresholds: green >=8 (including PHI pass), amber 6-7 (PHI pass required), red <=5 or PHI fail.

I'll upload the rubric spreadsheet to the Drive folder and link in the hubspot deal. Let me know if you want the SE team to run an initial dry-run against a 200-sample subset before the full 1k. I'd recommend it to surface obvious prompt issues quickly.

Cheers,
